policy: A translated primary text, a scholar's argument, a community self-description, a publisher abstract and an unverified quotation are different witnesses. Search-accessible excerpts are not represented as full-book readings. No original-language manuscript collation or survey of whole living communities was performed.

sources.title: Maimonides, Guide for the Perplexed III.22
sources.scope: The chapter's Job interpretation and discussion of Satan, inclination, death and permission were consulted. This is not a verbatim statement that all demonology was foreign to Judaism.

sources.title: Maimonides, Laws of Kings and Wars 11, translated by Eliyahu Touger
sources.scope: Messianic criteria, miracles and the criticism of Jesus were consulted. Translator explanations remain distinct from the medieval author.

sources.title: Job 1-2, World English Bible
sources.scope: Job 1:6-12 supplies the divine-council and permission comparison. Narrative setting is not adopted as a secure composition date.

sources.title: Isaiah 45, World English Bible
sources.scope: The Cyrus setting and verse 7 are the selected unit. No explicit reference to Zarathustra occurs in that verse; identifying a specific Iranian target is an interpretation.

sources.title: Jacques Duchesne-Guillemin, Dead Sea Scrolls, Encyclopaedia Iranica
sources.kind: Scholarly argument with translated primary excerpts
sources.scope: The reproduced Community Rule two-spirits passage and the author's Iranian-influence argument were read. The article's 1994 historical reconstruction is not treated as current consensus; unrelated identifications and older dating claims are not imported.

sources.title: Israel's angels and Qumran religious identity, Bible Interp, University of Arizona
sources.scope: Selected Community Rule and 11QMelchizedek comparisons and the distinction between sectarian and nonsectarian texts were consulted.

sources.title: John J. Collins and James Nati, The Rule of the Association and Related Texts (2024)
sources.scope: Description only, not the complete commentary. It distinguishes multiple settlements and manuscript forms and explicitly identifies Iranian-dualism comparison as a topic.

sources.title: Israel Museum, Digital Dead Sea Scrolls project
sources.scope: War and Temple scroll descriptions and material dating. No direct full-English translation of those manuscripts was retrieved from the project.

sources.title: War Scroll, Center for Online Judaic Studies
sources.scope: The opening conflict between the sons of light and darkness. The site's title date is not used as an independently settled date for all layers of the text.

sources.title: Jubilees 10, R. H. Charles translation
sources.kind: Primary text in an older translation
sources.scope: Mastema's petition and the retention of one tenth of the spirits, verses 8-9, were read in context. This is a distinct account from the Watchers story.

sources.title: Gherardo Gnoli, Dualism, Encyclopaedia Iranica
sources.scope: Differences among Gathic, later Zoroastrian and other dualistic formulations. This does not justify a single equal-two-gods formula for every Iranian tradition.

sources.title: Jacques Duchesne-Guillemin, Ahriman, Encyclopaedia Iranica
sources.scope: Changing relationships among destructive spirit, beneficent spirit and Ahura Mazda; not a uniform creed for all periods.

sources.title: Plato, Timaeus, translated by Benjamin Jowett
sources.scope: The creator's goodness and the ordered cosmos, conventionally located around 29e-30a. The argument does not equate all Platonism with hatred of matter.

sources.title: Tanya, Iggeret HaTeshuvah, chapter 6
sources.scope: Divine vitality, the other side and repentance. This is evidence for a particular later Jewish framework, not proof of direct transmission from Jesus or Qumran.

sources.title: To Do the Will of Our Father in Heaven, Orthodox rabbinic statement (2015)
sources.scope: Cooperation with Christians and retained theological differences. Signatories do not stand for all Orthodox or Hasidic Jews, and the statement does not endorse Christian dogma.

sources.title: Paul Mendes-Flohr on Martin Buber, ABC Philosophers Zone interview
sources.scope: Discussion of Buber's appreciation of Jesus. It is not a newly authenticated page from Two Types of Faith or evidence of a recent Hasidic movement.

sources.title: Daniel Boyarin, The Jewish Gospels, publisher description
sources.kind: Publisher account of a scholarly thesis
sources.scope: Jewish contexts of early Christological claims. The complete book was not read in this pass, and its argument is not identified with a consensus of all Jewish authorities.

sources.title: Israel Knohl, The Messiah Before Jesus, publisher description
sources.kind: Publisher account of a scholarly thesis
sources.scope: The proposed pre-Christian messianic interpretation is recorded as the author's argument, not a settled archaeological discovery or a demonstrated Jesus-Teacher identity.

sources.title: Charles G. Haeberl and James F. McGrath, The Mandaean Book of John: Text and Translation
sources.scope: Edition metadata and open-version description were read. The downloadable PDF returned an access error; no full critical edition or commentary reading is claimed.

sources.title: Edmondo Lupieri, Mandaeans i. History, Encyclopaedia Iranica
sources.kind: Scholarly history with explicit disputed-origin theories
sources.scope: Miriai's Jewish-priestly origin, transmission debates and the history of outside classifications. Lupieri's own preferred origin reconstruction is not treated as a settled community genealogy.

sources.title: Community response concerning translation of the Mandaean Book of John (2023)
sources.kind: Primary reception document and disputed translation
sources.scope: The response preserves Jewish-born Miriai while disputing features of an academic translation. It is one community-associated intervention, not a certified consensus translation.

sources.title: Mandaean Associations Union, Mandaean beliefs
sources.scope: Marriage, family and ritual commitments. Older population figures and universal statements about every adherent are not reused.

sources.title: Gospel of Philip, translated by Willis Barnstone
sources.scope: The five ritual mysteries and selected light/darkness passages were available through indexed text. Full direct-page access was unreliable; no Coptic collation is claimed.

sources.title: Treatise on the Resurrection, translated by Willis Barnstone
sources.scope: The passage affirming resurrection's reality and transformation was consulted in indexed text. The collection is Nag Hammadi Codex I,4; it does not simply reject resurrection.

sources.title: Ptolemy's Letter to Flora, G. R. S. Mead translation
sources.kind: Older translation transmitted through a polemical source
sources.scope: The intermediate, just lawgiver is the selected comparison. Ptolemy's letter is not itself a Nag Hammadi find; full surviving textual tradition was not collated.

sources.title: Gnosticism, Internet Encyclopedia of Philosophy
sources.scope: Distinct Sethian, Valentinian and related positions; the categories are not imposed as one self-described ancient religion.

sources.title: Werner Sundermann, Cosmogony and Cosmology iii. In Manicheism, Encyclopaedia Iranica
sources.scope: The two principles and the light powers' construction of a cosmos functioning in rescue. No claim that every physical structure was simply an evil creator's mistake.

sources.title: Manicheism i. General Survey, Encyclopaedia Iranica
sources.scope: Prophetic claims, community organization and transmitted scriptures. Elect/Hearers are not described as hereditary castes.

sources.title: Samyutta Nikaya 22.59, translation by Bhikkhu Bodhi
sources.scope: Nonself in relation to the five aggregates. This is not a metaphysical summary of every Buddhist school or a denial of all conventional personal agency.

sources.title: Baha'i international community, introductory teachings
sources.scope: Named Manifestations including Buddha and Zoroaster and progressive revelation. These are the faith's teachings, not independent proof of every historical identification.

sources.title: Ahmadiyya Muslim Community Greece, community and founder account
sources.scope: Explicit recognition of Buddha and Zoroaster and the 1889 origin. Promotional superlatives and membership counts are not adopted.

sources.title: Ahmadiyya Muslim Community, official introduction
sources.scope: Mirza Ghulam Ahmad of Qadian and foundation in 1889. Contemporary officeholders and membership estimates are not used.

sources.title: Common Declaration of Pope Paul VI and Pope Shenouda III, May 10, 1973
sources.scope: Triune faith and real humanity/divinity of Christ. This is not a claim that the two churches are institutionally reunited.

sources.title: CNEWA, The Catholic Eastern Churches
sources.scope: Church identities and communion categories. No current population or officeholder figures are reproduced.

sources.title: Karaite Jews of America, Reading Room
sources.scope: Commentary, law and liturgy show that rejection of rabbinic oral-law authority is not absence of interpretation or inherited practice.

sources.title: Samaritan Museum, About the Museum
sources.scope: The five-book Torah, priestly lineage and community heritage. Promotional claims to be oldest or smallest are not adopted as comparative facts.

sources.title: Christine Allison, Yazidis i. General, Encyclopaedia Iranica
sources.scope: Oral transmission and problems with purported sacred books. Outsider accusations about worship are not adopted, and older demographic figures are not reused.

sources.title: Druze doctrine and law, Institute of Ismaili Studies lecture description
sources.scope: Eleventh-century Fatimid setting and a distinctive developing tradition. The full video was not reviewed; no secret doctrines or Buddha/Zoroaster list is invented.

sources.title: Wilferd Madelung, Zaydiyya, Institute of Ismaili Studies
sources.scope: Origins in the movement associated with Zayd and distinctive imamship. The historical category is not a present political rating.

sources.title: Institute of Ismaili Studies, Ismaili community
sources.scope: Interpretation, imamship and cultural diversity. The description chiefly represents the Nizari institution; it is not every Ismaili branch's complete self-description.

sources.title: The Pluralism Project, dhikr
sources.scope: The meaning of remembrance and devotional practices. One practice does not make every Sufi order an identical denomination or theology.

sources.title: Latter-day Saints 101, official church introduction
sources.scope: Additional scripture and a Godhead account distinct from Nicene consubstantiality. Historical religious claims remain attributed.

sources.title: What Do Jehovah's Witnesses Believe?, official publication
sources.scope: Jesus as a created Son, rejection of the Trinity and biblical authority. The source's evaluation of other churches is not adopted.

sources.title: 1 John 2 and 4, World English Bible
sources.scope: The antichrist references in 2:18-23 are read with the incarnation test of 4:1-3. The Gospel of John and the epistles are distinct works.

sources.title: 2 John, World English Bible
sources.scope: Verse 7's language about Jesus Christ coming in flesh. It is not a generic definition covering every doubt about every miracle.

sources.title: Quran 4:157-171, translated text
sources.scope: The passage rejects opponents' killing/crucifying claim and includes the warning against saying Three. Later explanations of precisely what happened are not all identical to its wording.

sources.title: Philippians 2, World English Bible
sources.scope: Verses 5-11 combine exalted portrayal, obedient agency and divine exaltation. This is a control against locating all high Christology only in the Gospel of John.

sources.title: Matthew 12, World English Bible
sources.scope: Verses 24-29 connect exorcism, Satan's kingdom and God's arriving reign. This supports contextual comparison, not automatic authentication of every narrated event.

sources.title: Luke 22, World English Bible
sources.scope: Verse 31's requested testing and the prayer sequence. These portrayals do not imply a second uncreated creator.
